notes: ZERO FLIPS, score-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION — the bit-identity gate, not a hope. This cycle adds principal chains (decoration) to clause-side atom instances and changes nothing else; under the S1 decoration-blind join (baseline snapshot decoration-blind-join-2026-08-04, pricing_version 1.2 via overlay_empty.json, the exact keep config this cycle reuses), the atom-channel match key, the atom df/idf, and the lexical atom-text all read the DECHAINED name (polarity + stem, chain stripped), so adding a chain changes no match key, no df entry, no lex document — chains are pricing metadata invisible to every channel. THE GATE TEST THAT PINS IT: test_dechain.py::test_add_chain_mutant_leaves_every_channel_score_bit_identical (a planted add-chain mutant must leave every channel score bit-identical under the v1.2 index; it was verified RED against the legacy exact-name join, where the same mutant moves scores — S1's review re-planted its own mutant and watched 8 named tests go red). Any flip observed at MEASURE therefore falsifies the JOIN contract, not the backfill: it is a BUG in the v1.2 dechained join, the cycle halts, and the S1 cycle reopens. Nothing in this cycle is adjudicated by flips because nothing may move; the judgment content lives in the seat's verdict file and its independent review of both verdict directions (chain_licensed sampled AND no_chain_licensed sampled, plus 100% of landings on sensitive clauses), which is where review effort goes. expected_directions is the honest empty list (legal iff max == 0); max_regressions 0 for the same reason.
